words.definition: Lasting for a very short time; transitory. Often used of things whose brevity is part of their appeal.
words.example: The ephemeral beauty of cherry blossoms draws crowds each spring.

words.definition: Using very few words; terse to the point of seeming brusque.
words.example: Her laconic reply — "Fine." — ended the discussion.

words.definition: Present, appearing, or found everywhere at once.
words.example: Smartphones have become so ubiquitous that a quiet train carriage is now rare.

words.definition: The realization that each passerby is living a life as vivid and complex as your own. A coined word, now in informal use.
words.example: Watching lit windows from the night bus, he felt a sudden wave of sonder.

words.definition: The pleasant, earthy smell that follows rain falling on dry ground.
words.example: The first storm of the season filled the street with petrichor.

words.definition: To make something obscure, unclear, or harder to understand, often deliberately.
words.example: The report seemed designed to obfuscate rather than explain where the money went.

words.definition: Having a ready insight into and understanding of things; sharply perceptive.
words.example: A perspicacious editor caught the flaw in the argument before anyone else did.

words.definition: Truthful and straightforward, even when the truth is uncomfortable.
words.example: I'd rather have a candid answer than a polite one.

words.definition: Able to recover quickly from difficulty; tough and springy.
words.example: Children are often more resilient than the adults around them expect.

words.definition: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.
words.example: She kept meticulous records of every expense.

words.definition: Dealing with things in a practical, realistic way rather than according to theory or ideals.
words.example: We took the pragmatic route and shipped the simpler version first.

words.definition: Open to more than one interpretation; not having one obvious meaning.
words.example: The instructions were ambiguous enough that half the team did it differently.

words.definition: Fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing.
words.example: His eloquent toast left half the room in tears.

words.definition: Showing steady, careful effort in one's work or duties.
words.example: A diligent reviewer reads the footnotes too.

words.definition: Well-meaning and kindly; wishing others well.
words.example: The benevolent landlord froze rents through the winter.

words.definition: To examine something very closely and critically.
words.example: Auditors will scrutinize every invoice from that quarter.

words.definition: To make suffering, a problem, or a burden less severe.
words.example: A cold compress can alleviate the swelling.

words.definition: General agreement among a group.
words.example: After an hour the team reached a consensus on the launch date.

words.definition: A subtle difference in meaning, expression, or tone.
words.example: Translation loses the nuance of a joke long before it loses the words.

words.definition: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another person.
words.example: Good nurses combine competence with empathy.

words.definition: Certain to happen; unavoidable.
words.example: Once the dam cracked, the flood was inevitable.

words.definition: More than is needed or wanted; unnecessary.
words.example: The editor cut every superfluous adjective from the opening page.

words.definition: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.
words.example: Gossip has a pernicious way of poisoning a small office.

words.definition: To use ambiguous language so as to avoid committing oneself.
words.example: Asked whether layoffs were coming, the CEO equivocated for ten minutes.

words.definition: Intended for or understood by only a small group with specialised knowledge.
words.example: The lecture drifted into esoteric details about lattice symmetry.

words.definition: To place two things side by side, especially to highlight contrast.
words.example: The exhibit juxtaposes war photographs with children's drawings.

words.definition: Generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival or someone less powerful.
words.example: In a magnanimous gesture, the champion praised her opponent's game.

words.definition: A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds.
words.example: The market at dawn was a cacophony of horns, gulls and shouted prices.

words.definition: To make a bad situation better.
words.example: Flexible hours did a lot to ameliorate staff burnout.

words.definition: Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way but with harmful effects.
words.example: Hearing loss is insidious; most people notice it years late.

words.definition: A typical example or pattern of something; a model that frames how a field thinks.
words.example: Plate tectonics replaced an older paradigm of a fixed Earth.

words.definition: Producing a great deal of something, especially creative work.
words.example: A prolific songwriter, she released three albums in two years.

words.definition: Holding firmly to something; persistent and determined.
words.example: The tenacious reporter kept calling until someone answered.

words.definition: To regard with deep respect or reverence.
words.example: The village still venerates the teacher who founded its school.

words.definition: Based on personal whim or chance rather than reason or a system.
words.example: The deadline felt arbitrary — nobody could say why it was Tuesday.

words.definition: Something that speeds up a change or reaction without being consumed by it.
words.example: The blackout became a catalyst for the city's grid overhaul.

words.definition: Based on observation or experiment rather than theory alone.
words.example: The claim sounds plausible, but there is no empirical evidence for it.

words.definition: To use something to its maximum advantage.
words.example: The startup leveraged its mailing list to fund the first print run.

words.definition: To make something less severe, serious, or painful.
words.example: Sandbags mitigated the worst of the flooding.

words.definition: Something that deviates from what is standard, normal, or expected.
words.example: One warm week in January is an anomaly, not a trend.

words.definition: The combination of separate parts or ideas into a coherent whole.
words.example: Her thesis is a synthesis of economics and ecology.

words.definition: A person who flatters powerful people to gain advantage.
words.example: Surrounded by sycophants, the director never heard bad news in time.

words.definition: Excessively eager to please or obey; fawning.
words.example: The obsequious waiter refilled our glasses after every sip.

words.definition: Too great or extreme to be expressed in words.
words.example: Standing under the aurora, she felt an ineffable calm.

words.definition: Given to using long words; or, of a word, having many syllables.
words.example: His sesquipedalian emails took twice as long to read as to answer.

words.definition: Exceedingly idealistic; unrealistic and impractical in pursuit of a noble goal.
words.example: It was a quixotic plan: one van, no budget, and a promise to feed the whole town.

words.definition: Physical beauty. An ugly-sounding word for a lovely thing.
words.example: The poem praises the pulchritude of a face the poet saw only once.

words.definition: The act of throwing someone or something out of a window. Also used jokingly for abrupt dismissal.
words.example: The board's swift defenestration of the founder shocked investors.

words.definition: The warmth of the sun in winter. An old word, rarely used but often missed.
words.example: We ate lunch on the frozen steps for the apricity alone.

words.definition: An involuntary state of intense romantic infatuation and obsessive longing for another person.
words.example: Psychologists distinguish limerence from the steadier attachment of long relationships.

words.definition: Stubbornly uncooperative toward authority or discipline.
words.example: The recalcitrant printer refused every driver we tried.

words.definition: Carried out with minimal effort or reflection; done as a routine duty.
words.example: The inspection was perfunctory — two minutes and a signature.

words.definition: The appearance of being true or real.
words.example: The novel's verisimilitude comes from a hundred small, accurate details.

words.definition: The partially shaded outer region of a shadow; by extension, a grey area at the edge of something.
words.example: The rule lives in a legal penumbra where nobody is quite sure it applies.

words.definition: The defining spirit or mood of a particular period of history.
words.example: The film caught the zeitgeist of the late nineties almost by accident.

words.definition: Denoting a period of the past that was idyllically happy and peaceful.
words.example: They still talk about the halcyon summers before the factory closed.

words.definition: Fond of company; sociable.
words.example: A gregarious host, he introduced every guest to three others within minutes.

words.definition: Sparing or economical with money or food.
words.example: Frugal habits from her student years never quite left her.

words.definition: A proposed explanation made on limited evidence, used as a starting point for further investigation.
words.example: Our hypothesis is that the leak starts when the pump overheats.

words.definition: Expressed clearly and easy to understand; also, thinking clearly.
words.example: The manual is unusually lucid for a piece of technical writing.

words.definition: Able to adapt to many different functions or activities.
words.example: A cast-iron pan is the most versatile thing in my kitchen.
